population.note: FICTIONAL. Of ~274M adults, 32.5% current ≈ 89.1M; 43.5% ever ≈ 119.2M; used-and-off-now 11.0% ≈ 30.1M; never-used ≈ 155M. Cycling arithmetic: ever 43.5 − current 32.5 = 11.0 pts off now. About 15.5 pts of current users are on a second or later course and about 4.5 pts of the off-now group restarted and stopped again, so (15.5+4.5)/43.5 ≈ 46% cycled. This is consistent with ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% one-year restart: the 2033 pen recall forced several million injectable users off for 4–16 weeks, and most restarted on Foundayo, which turned forced stops into recorded cycles. Ever-use rose 8.0 pts (envelope limit 10.5) and current use rose 7.5. Age check: 18–29 19% × 52M = 9.9M; 30–49 38% × 91M = 34.6M; 50–64 47% × 61M = 28.7M; 65+ 23% × 70M = 16.1M; total ≈ 89.2M ≈ 32.5%. Three groups account for the new users. (1) Needle refusers moved to high-dose Foundayo once it matched injectable semaglutide. (2) About 3.9M adults without obesity take 'metabolic health' or longevity regimens, mostly top-third and 30–64. (3) About 1.6M started for alcohol after the 2034 guideline endorsement, often through EAP referral, which skews younger and male. The 18–29 rise from 13.5% to 19% comes mostly from 'focus' subscriptions, AUD referrals and imported pens. The bottom third went from 21% to 28.5%. Medicaid enrolment in the same 31 states plus DC accounts for about half of that, and imported or counterfeit product for most of the rest. The bottom third is therefore the group most exposed to the 2033–34 contamination cluster. Imported/counterfeit users ≈ 8.5M, up from 3.8M, and are under-measured. Never-users (~155M) are now mostly under-30, rural residents of non-expansion states, people with contraindications, and refusers by conviction. Off-now (30.1M) includes ≈2.1M on CMS bone pauses or medically advised pauses, ≈4M cut off by gated plans, and ≈1.5M who stopped after the 2034 anhedonia label and say so. Pediatric: 1.1% of ~73M ≈ 800k, mostly adolescents 12+. Some under-12 use continues under specialists, and adolescent oral use is growing because Foundayo needs no injection teaching. About two children in five now live with at least one parent who is on the drug or cycling.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Structure unchanged (status quo). The permanent Part D obesity benefit continues: BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with one comorbidity, at the statutory $199 negotiated rate with a $50 copay and the counselling visit. The rate is locked under the 2031 contracts through Dec 2035. Medicare pays 19.7% of users ≈ 17.6M (16.1M aged 65+ plus ≈1.5M disabled under-65): ≈6.5M diabetes and ≈11.1M obesity. Obesity-benefit gross at full adherence: 11.1M × $199 × 12 ≈ $26.5B. Beneficiary copays: 11.1M × $50 × 12 ≈ $6.7B, leaving ≈$19.8B net to the program. All Medicare incretin users: 17.6M × $199 × 12 ≈ $42.0B gross. Medicaid: still 31 states plus DC at the 90% enhanced match under the continuation standard, with no new adopters and no withdrawals. Medicaid pays 14.0% ≈ 12.5M × $199 × 12 ≈ $29.9B gross before supplemental rebates. The obesity net of ≈$19.8B/yr runs above the CBO's ≈$14B/yr ten-year average because 65+ uptake beat the score. Public payers are shielded from the 2033 price shock by the locked rate. Commercial and cash buyers are not.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands at $5–30/month, generic oral semaglutide, and grey 'research' tirzepatide and retatrutide made from Chinese API at $40–90/month. China: domestic generic semaglutide and tirzepatide copies, and its API remains the backbone of the global gray trade. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 50–80/month. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt have generics. In the US, the settled 2033 semaglutide entry did not happen. The lead filer received a Complete Response after FDA found data-integrity failures at its Hyderabad site, and the second filer's settlement rights depend on the first launch. Entry now looks like 2035 at the earliest. Tirzepatide exclusivity runs later.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Shock up. Three things combined: a Feb 2033 sterility recall and line halt at Lilly's North Carolina fill-finish site, the failed 2033 generic semaglutide entry, and a Section 232 increase on branded pharmaceutical imports from 15% to 25% (Apr 2033). Portal prices for injectables rose from $199–279 to $279–379. Retatrutide went to $499 direct and $1,649 list, and amycretin to $499. Orals: the Foundayo and Wegovy pill starting doses stay at $149 on the federal direct portal as a political anchor, and maintenance and high doses rose from $199 to $229–249. Commercial PBM net rose from ≈$170–190 to ≈$215–235. Employer pharmacy trend is ≈+12%, and coverage slipped from 66% to 64% as some mid-size employers dropped coverage or moved to oral-only formularies. Payer mix of ≈89.2M users: commercial 34.8% (31.0M), Medicare 19.7% (17.6M), Medicaid 14.0% (12.5M), cash/direct 22.0% (19.6M, including ≈4.6M 'calm'/'focus' subscribers and ≈3.9M longevity/'metabolic health' users), imported/counterfeit 9.5% (8.5M). Sum 89.2M = 100%. Route: ≈55% of users are on daily orals. Injectables are now mostly retatrutide, amycretin, CagriSema and Medicare semaglutide inertia. ≈75% of covering employers are gated, and many gated plans now require Foundayo first. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand, so the shortage listing did not reopen compounding. US paid market at full-adherence rates ≈ Medicare $42.0B + Medicaid $29.9B + commercial 31.0M × $225 × 12 ≈ $83.7B + cash 19.6M × $230 × 12 ≈ $54.1B ≈ $210B gross.

GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro), supply restored late 2033
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance; FDA shortage list Feb 2033–Jan 2034)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 small-molecule, daily oral (orforglipron: Foundayo, incl. 48 mg high-dose maintenance approved Sep 2033)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: alcohol use disorder: guideline-endorsed second-line (ASAM and VA/DoD guidelines, 2034), not yet FDA-labelled; semaglutide sNDA filed Jul 2034
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'metabolic health' and longevity regimens for adults without obesity (≈3.9M), sold as low-dose Foundayo 'maintenance' through concierge practices, longevity clinic chains and retail-pharmacy telehealth
'calm', 'focus' and 'craving freedom' subscriptions (≈4.6M), still in employer lifestyle catalogues but now carrying the anhedonia boxed text
alcohol reduction via EAP referral, now on-guideline
smoking and vaping cessation (trial reading out 2035)
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The oral_parity driver is met by an existing product in a new form. No novel oral was in late-stage review in the parent world. In Sep 2033 FDA approved a 48 mg Foundayo maintenance dose after a 72-week head-to-head trial showed 16.4% mean loss against 16.1% for injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg, which is non-inferior. A pill now matches the most-prescribed injectable. It does not match tirzepatide's ~21% or retatrutide 12 mg's 30%, and the top tier is still a pen. Foundayo is a small molecule made in Lilly's US plants, so it avoided both the fill-finish failure and the import tariff, and it became the default rescue for recalled pen users. Its ~1–2 day half-life also makes weekend drug holidays possible, which oral semaglutide's week-long half-life does not. Survodutide was approved Mar 2033 as a weekly injectable for chronic weight management and MASH-adjacent use, with no new standalone indication. MariTide was approved Oct 2033 on 72-week DEXA data with a bone-monitoring label. Monthly dosing is used mainly in Medicare Advantage clinics, and supply is small. Bimagrumab combinations: a filing was made Jun 2034, and approval cannot come before mid-2035. AUD: a Novo sNDA was filed Jul 2034 on two phase 3 heavy-drinking-day trials, with a decision in 2035. The 2034 guideline endorsement is what counts as honouring the driver. FDA class labelling for reward blunting was added Mar 2034. No new FDA indication this step.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect. A new pattern is restart nausea after weekend Foundayo holidays and recall-forced gaps. ED visits for vomiting rose during the 2033 restart wave.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained. Foundayo label adds re-titration guidance after gaps longer than 3 days.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Absolute numbers keep rising with the larger 65+ population and high-dose triple-agonist use.
No causal confirmation. Counterfeit retatrutide cases badly confound 2033–34 reporting.

≈1.7M long-term users aged 65+ meet sarcopenia criteria (updated Medicare claims estimate, 2034). Lean mass is ~30–40% of loss in untrained users over 50. A new concern is normal-BMI longevity users losing lean mass from an already lean starting point.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label retained. Body-composition monitoring is in the retatrutide 12 mg, amycretin and MariTide labels. The CMS annual DEXA requirement continues.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈8.0M users aged 65+ now have more than 2 years' use. 8.0M × ~0.6%/yr hip-fracture baseline × 0.35 excess ≈ 16,800 excess hip fractures a year against ~305,000 US total, plus vertebral fractures among cycling postmenopausal women. DEXA waits ease slightly to 8–16 weeks as mobile capacity grows, but demand keeps rising.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelling retained; bone endpoints required in filings; the CMS 90-day bone-pause code continues; private gated plans are still not bound by it. The DOJ civil case against Novo is unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention; no class determination.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association. Re-examined in the 2034 anhedonia review and still not supported.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FDA's March 2034 class labelling cites pooled trial SHAPS data and the retatrutide postmarketing study. Clinically meaningful anhedonia was seen in ~12% of retatrutide 12 mg users vs ~5% of comparators, ~8–9% at top-dose tirzepatide or semaglutide 7.2 mg, and ~5–6% at low-dose oral vs ~4–5% placebo, so the risk is dose-dependent. With ≈9M on top-dose regimens that implies roughly 400–600k excess cases. Among low-dose 'calm'/'focus' users the excess is small per person but spread across ≈4.6M people. Usually reversible within 2–6 weeks of dose reduction.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Added to the Adverse Reactions and Warnings sections of all incretin labels, with a prevalence table and dose-reduction advice. A Medication Guide is required at dispensing, including for 'calm'/'focus' telehealth brands. No boxed warning. The existing FTC consent orders remain.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The 2033 pen recall added several million forced-stop regain episodes on top of the usual gating, pause and anhedonia-driven stops.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The CMS bone-pause code softens it for Medicare. The CMS also allowed recall gaps to count as covered days for PDC (sub-regulatory guidance, Mar 2033). The Seventh Circuit has not ruled on the Indiana waiver.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D, calcium and protein insufficiency in high-loss older users. Similar patterns now appear in normal-BMI longevity users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; Part D counselling template screen; no FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of follow-up. The adolescent BMD subset signal persists in a second interim look and is still underpowered. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use, and weekend holidays are a new, unstudied cycling pattern.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; full adolescent data due 2034 are delayed to 2035 by sponsor request.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: This is now a public-health story. With ≈8.5M users on imported or counterfeit product, poison-centre incretin calls rose ~2.4× from 2032. Most involve 10× dosing errors from mislabelled 'research' vials. The Nov 2033–Feb 2034 cluster of Burkholderia and endotoxin contamination in counterfeit retatrutide vials caused ≈410 hospitalisations and 27 deaths across 12 states, concentrated in Phoenix, Kansas City and the Rio Grande Valley.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CDC Health Alert Network advisories, CBP parcel seizures up sharply, and FDA import alerts on 40+ Indian and Chinese suppliers. The 'Safe Pens' bill is still stalled. Individuals are still not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in 65+ users with more than 2 years' use and track the sarcopenia estimate.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Mandatory fall-risk screening in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The 2033 recall gave researchers a natural experiment. Forced 8–16-week gaps in users over 50 produced measurable visceral-fat rebound on repeat DEXA.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Joint guidance update 2034 recommends resistance training during any gap; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A mean resting heart-rate rise of several bpm at 12 mg; arrhythmia significance unclear. Counterfeit 'reta' overdoses produce tachycardia ED presentations.

safety_ledger.effect: Underweight and energy deficiency in normal-BMI 'metabolic health' users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. Sports-medicine and eating-disorder clinics report BMI <18.5, amenorrhoea and stress fractures among women aged 20–40 on low-dose longevity or 'focus' regimens. No population estimate yet.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Eating-disorder society advisory (2034); no FDA action because the use is off-label.

food_and_beverage.state: With a third of adults on the drug, US salty-snack volume is falling ~5% a year and confectionery ~6%. Sugary drinks keep sliding. A third large packaged-food group sold its snack brands to private equity in 2033. Protein and 'bone-forward' fortified lines still lead growth, and Foundayo pharmacy displays sit next to them. Some savings from lower volume go into smaller-pack premium formats at higher unit prices.

alcohol.state: Seventh straight year of US spirits volume decline, now ~6% a year. Beer is down ~3%. After the 2034 ASAM guideline, EAP-referred prescribing for drinking is mainstream, and distributors in Milwaukee and Louisville have announced consolidations. Non-alcoholic and 'one good drink' premium formats still hold.

restaurants.state: Spend per cover in high-uptake suburbs is ~12% below 2028. Bar revenue is the line that hurt most. Half portions and gram pricing are standard. 'Friday-off' tasting menus have appeared, timed to Foundayo weekend holidays. Atlanta and Memphis no-gram rooms and chain 'full table' nights persist.

apparel.state: The 2033 recall caused a sudden size-up wave, and resale platforms reported record mid-size inventory. Cycling-sized rental keeps growing, and mid-market plus ranges keep shrinking.

fitness.state: Still growing. Gap-period 'hold your muscle' programmes boomed during the recall. 'Prescribed lifting' in MA and DEXA-plus-coaching chains are expanding, and longevity clinics bundle lifting with low-dose Foundayo. The binding constraint is still trainers qualified for older clients.

insurance.state: Employer pharmacy trend is ~+12% after the price rise, and coverage slipped to 64%. Gated plans increasingly require Foundayo first. Medicare is shielded by the $199 lock until Dec 2035 and is already budgeting for renegotiation. Life insurers keep asking untreated applicants with BMI ≥30 why. Disability carriers have begun adding anhedonia to mental-health claim review templates.

pharma.state: Revenue is up on both volume and commercial price. Lilly dominates through Foundayo, whose high dose rescued the recall year, and is negotiating an FDA consent arrangement on its North Carolina site. Novo keeps Medicare semaglutide share and has the AUD filing. Its generic exposure was deferred by the Hyderabad Complete Response. Amgen (MariTide) and Boehringer (survodutide) are small new entrants. Indian and Chinese makers dominate abroad and in the grey US trade.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Normalised further. Among insured adults over 35, being on it is the default, and the daily pill makes it as unremarkable as a vitamin. Being off needs a reason: 'bone pause', 'my plan', 'the grey' (newly acceptable since the label), or 'by conviction'. The 2033 recall regain is remembered collectively as 'the spring everyone got big again'. Trained shoulders still signal a well-run regimen, and very lean young women on longevity regimens are now a recognisable and worrying look on Los Angeles and Austin campuses.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use rates have nearly converged (bottom 28.5% vs top 36%), but risk has not. The top third takes branded Foundayo 48 mg or retatrutide with DEXA and coaching, and runs longevity regimens without obesity. The bottom third is on Medicaid continuation standards or on imported vials. The 2033–34 contamination deaths fell mostly on uninsured and non-expansion-state users in Arizona, Missouri and Texas.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first meals are the norm. Hosts now also plan around Friday-night and Saturday 'off' guests on drug holidays, who arrive hungry. The weekend shared meal has partly come back as a weekly appetite window, while weekday dinners stay small. Church potlucks and no-gram rooms continue.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps add a 'holiday days' field next to on/off. 'Unmedicated' remains a niche filter. Advice columns now field complaints about partners who are only themselves on weekends.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is treated as something to switch off on weekdays and allow on weekends. The backlash coalition is the same size and proportionally smaller. It gained energy from the counterfeit deaths and the anhedonia label, and its framing has moved from 'weigh-in welfare' to 'they knew about the grey'.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Labelled since March 2034: excess clinically meaningful anhedonia runs from ~1 pt at low-dose oral to ~7 pts at retatrutide 12 mg. Applied to ≈89M users with ≈9M on top doses, that implies roughly 400–600k excess top-dose cases plus a diffuse low-dose tail of perhaps 300–500k. Surveys (Pew-style, 2034) find ~40% of current users have deliberately taken a 'drug holiday' in the past year, mostly weekend Foundayo skips. Dose step-downs to recover 'colour' are the second most common reason for a prescription change, after GI effects.
interior_life.framing: Side effect, named and managed. The label turned 'the grey' from a vendor-softened feature into a common complaint with a known remedy: dose down, or take Saturdays off. 'Quiet' and 'Even' still sell, now with a Medication Guide in the box, and their marketing has shifted to 'your dial'. Clinicians ask 'how's your colour?' at follow-ups.
interior_life.effect_on_work: White-collar employers kept 'focus' subscriptions in lifestyle catalogues, but two large platforms added the label text and an opt-out prompt. Sales, hospitality and creative workers schedule holidays before pitches and service peaks. Fleets and warehouses push for continuous use, and unions argue that weekend holidays are a private medical choice. Medicaid and Part D users can only take holidays by filling and skipping, because the continuation standard measures fills, not ingestion. Skipped pills are piling up in cabinets.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: The 'grey era' has become a mainstream critical label, and 'Saturday records' (music written on holiday days) is a recognised Nashville and Atlanta marketing tag. Comedy about 'the grey' plays in arenas. Saturday-night venues, spicy food and extreme sports keep gaining.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Weekend holidays sync couples' desire to Friday–Sunday, and therapists describe 'weekday roommates'. Pharmacies sell anti-nausea 'Monday packs' for the restart. Partners in mixed-dose couples now negotiate holiday calendars.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The anhedonia label started a mass tort that plaintiffs' firms are building from 2031 consent-order documents. Senate hearings on the counterfeit deaths produced no law. The approaching Medicare repricing in 2035 is the next budget fight. Talk of 'calm voters' and turnout is still unproven.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding and reactive. It added class anhedonia labelling, approved Foundayo 48 mg, MariTide and survodutide with bone monitoring, issued a Complete Response on the lead generic semaglutide filer, and put retatrutide on the shortage list without reopening compounding. Import enforcement is louder (more seizures, 40+ import alerts), but there is still no importation law and no individual prosecutions. There was no new conditioning action this step.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Unchanged: a permanent Part D obesity benefit at $199 with a $50 copay, and a 90% federal Medicaid match in the same 31 states plus DC. The $199 rate is locked through Dec 2035. No individual mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The CMS continuation standard is unchanged: ≥80% PDC from claims, six-monthly verified weights, ≥5% response or clinician override, annual DEXA for long-term 65+, and a 90-day bone pause. The only change is sub-regulatory guidance counting recall gaps as covered days. Indiana and Arkansas 12-month rules continue. Private gating covers ~75% of employer plans, and wellness surcharges continue. Because the standard counts fills, it does not see pills that are filled and not taken.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT screening still pushes drivers toward tirzepatide, and many fleets moved drivers to Foundayo during the recall. The VA adopted GLP-1 second-line for AUD in its 2034 guideline. The Army accession debate is unresolved, and the Air Force waiver stands.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Section 232 pharma tariffs rose to 25% in Apr 2033 and are cited in every price increase. Foundayo's US small-molecule supply chain is held up politically as the model. Chinese API underlies both Indian generics abroad and counterfeit 'reta' vials at home. The US–India framework is strained by the Hyderabad findings.

events.event: FDA inspectors find sterility failures at Lilly's North Carolina fill-finish site. Lilly halts the line and recalls lots of Zepbound and retatrutide pens, and FDA lists retatrutide 12 mg as in shortage. Several million patients are switched to pills or go without for weeks.

The settled 2033 generic semaglutide launch fails. FDA issues a Complete Response to the lead filer after finding data-integrity problems at its Hyderabad plant. With a new 25% Section 232 tariff in force, Novo and Lilly raise direct-portal injectable prices to $279–379. Medicare's $199 rate is locked until the end of 2035.

FDA approves a 48 mg Foundayo maintenance dose after a head-to-head trial shows 16.4% weight loss against 16.1% for injectable semaglutide. Gated plans start requiring the pill first, and by mid-2034 more than half of users take a daily tablet.

CDC issues a health alert on counterfeit retatrutide vials sold as 'research peptides' after contamination and tenfold dosing errors. By February the cluster totals about 410 hospitalisations and 27 deaths in 12 states, concentrated in Phoenix, Kansas City and the Rio Grande Valley. The Safe Pens bill stays in committee.

FDA adds reward blunting and anhedonia to every incretin label, with a dose-response prevalence table running from about one extra case in 100 at low oral doses to seven in 100 at retatrutide 12 mg. Telehealth 'calm' brands must hand out a Medication Guide, and weekend 'drug holidays' become standard practice and part of clinic conversation.

ASAM and the VA/DoD endorse GLP-1 drugs as second-line treatment for alcohol use disorder, and Novo files a semaglutide AUD application a month later. That summer a national retail-pharmacy telehealth service and two longevity clinic chains launch low-dose 'metabolic maintenance' Foundayo plans for adults without obesity, reaching about 3.9M users by year-end.

open_tensions: Medicare's $199 rate expires in December 2035. Commercial net is now $215–235 and portal injectables $279–379, generic semaglutide has slipped to 2035 at best, and Medicare spends ≈$42B a year on incretins. The renegotiation, and whether it is scored with the fracture costs billed to Part A, is the next budget fight.

About 8.5M Americans use imported or counterfeit product after a cluster that killed 27 people. Seizures have risen, but Congress has neither legalised import nor passed Safe Pens. The people most exposed are the bottom third in non-expansion states.

The continuation standard counts pharmacy fills, not pills taken. Weekend drug holidays recommended to manage labelled anhedonia show up as full adherence. Skipped tablets are accumulating in home cabinets, being shared and diverted, and the rules cannot see any of it.

Labelled anhedonia now applies to ≈8.5M people without obesity on 'focus' and longevity regimens, plus a growing AUD population. A mass tort is forming, and an emerging energy-deficiency signal in lean young women has no regulator, because the use is off-label.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is on the US market; generic_us remains false.
The Part D obesity benefit pays the $199 negotiated rate with a $50 beneficiary copay for BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with one comorbidity, including the counselling visit.

The CMS continuation standard (≥80% PDC, six-monthly verified weights, 5% response threshold, annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users, 90-day 'bone pause' code) is unchanged, and the same 31 states plus DC use it for Medicaid at the 90% match.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx).
The suicidal-ideation warning removed in January 2026 has not returned, and the 503B exclusion and 503A compounding injunction still stand.

prose.headline: The Pill Caught Up, the Pens Ran Out, and a Third of America Now Takes Saturdays Off
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 one American adult in three takes an incretin drug, and most of them take it as a pill. Being on it is unremarkable, and being off it is what needs an explanation. The list of acceptable explanations got longer this year when the FDA printed one of them on the label.

The growth did not come from cheaper drugs. Prices went up. In February 2033 inspectors found sterility failures at Lilly's fill-finish plant in North Carolina, and pens for the strongest drugs were recalled within days. Retatrutide went on the shortage list for most of a year. In June, the generic semaglutide launch that every budget office had been waiting for did not happen, because the FDA rejected the lead filer's Hyderabad plant. With a new 25 percent tariff in force, the portal prices for injectables rose to $279 to $379 a month. Medicare was protected by its locked $199 rate, and so was Medicaid in the thirty-one states and D.C. that use it. Employers and cash buyers were not, and a few employers dropped coverage.

The pill filled the gap. In September the FDA approved a high maintenance dose of Lilly's Foundayo that matched injectable semaglutide in a head-to-head trial. It is a small molecule made in Indiana, unaffected by the tariff and the clean-room failure, and it became the default for recalled pen patients and then for gated plans. Retatrutide's thirty percent still requires a needle. But for most people the needle is gone, and with it the last practical reason not to start.

The shortage also opened space for an unregulated market. About eight and a half million Americans now inject imported generics or 'research' vials of retatrutide copied from Chinese ingredients. Last winter a run of contaminated and mislabelled vials put about four hundred people in hospital and killed twenty-seven, mostly in Phoenix, Kansas City and the Rio Grande Valley. There were Senate hearings. The bill to authenticate pens is still in committee, and nobody who bought a vial has been charged.

In March the FDA added reward blunting to every incretin label, with a table of rates: about one extra case of clinically meaningful anhedonia per hundred users at low oral doses, and about seven at the top pen dose. The label did not drive many people off the drug. Instead the response became an ordinary routine. Foundayo leaves the body in a day or two, so millions of people skip Friday and Saturday to get their colour back and restart on Sunday with a nausea pack. Restaurants run Friday-off tasting menus, and Nashville labels sell 'Saturday records'. Couples therapists talk about weekday roommates. On Medicaid and Part D, adherence is measured by pharmacy fills, so the skipped pills still count as taken and are piling up in kitchen cabinets.

The drug has also moved beyond weight. Addiction physicians and the VA now recommend it as second-line treatment for drinking, and employee assistance programmes refer to it routinely. Distributors in Milwaukee and Louisville are consolidating. Retail pharmacy telehealth and longevity clinics sell low-dose 'metabolic maintenance' to people who were never heavy, and sports-medicine clinics in Austin and Los Angeles are seeing young women who have become too thin. Nobody regulates that, because the use is off-label.

The older users have the same problems as before, on a larger scale. Eight million people over sixty-five have been on the drug for more than two years, and the excess hip fractures now come to roughly seventeen thousand a year. The drug is still billed to Part D and the fractures to Part A. Medicare's $199 contract expires at the end of 2035, and the manufacturers have already said what they expect.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Reyes takes her last Foundayo of the week at 6:10 on Thursday morning, standing at the sink in Mesa, and puts the blister pack behind the coffee so she won't reach for it tomorrow. It is the 48. Her dental group's plan made her switch off the pen during the recall, and it costs her a $45 copay now.

At work she cleans eleven mouths. Two patients ask about her weekend. One says, 'Off days?' and Marisol says, 'Off days,' and they both laugh like it's the weather.

At lunch she drives her mother to the DEXA van parked behind Our Lady of Guadalupe. Her mother is on a Medicare bone pause and keeps her coverage. In the van's waiting tent a man from the parish is telling people his nephew is still in Banner Desert after a vial from a website. Nobody asks which website. Everyone already knows the name.

Friday night her husband Ray grills. He is on Even, which his employer's catalogue covers, and he is off it tonight too. The smell of the carne asada hits her harder than anything has all week. She eats two tortillas and then a third, and Ray puts on the old Selena record and actually dances.

Sunday morning she takes the pill with the anti-nausea tablet from the Monday pack. By noon the kitchen goes quiet again and the colour drains out, and she wipes down the counter and texts her sister about Thanksgiving portions.
